text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Danish companies are missing out on vast export earnings as most Danish and European Union subsidies cover farming and industry exports and not Denmark's increasing exports of services.
--- U.S. medical group Boston Scientific is to close its Danish plant west of Copenhagen, dismissing 258 employees. Boston is moving to Ireland due to lower taxes and larger European Union subsidies.

--- New investments in excess of one million crowns are necessary to ensure that the Great Belt bridge-tunnel, road-rail fixed link meets maximum safety requirements, a report says. The Great Belt fixed link between Denmark's two biggest islands of Zealand, on which Copenhagen stands, and Funen is to open for passenger trains in June.
--- The European Commission has decided to grant 400 million crowns in subsidies to Denmark's economically depressed North Jutland region from 1997-1999, hoping to create 2,000 new jobs.
